summary: The UK, Canadian, Australian and Italian governments say their citizens need a visa for the DR Congo, obtained before travel. The immigration service's eVisa portal (evisa.gouv.cd) is open to any foreigner wishing to come for a visit and tourism, and entitles the holder to a 7-day airport visa, extendable, at any DRC entry point; no official source we could read states which nationalities need a visa. The UK government says a yellow fever vaccination certificate is required to enter, and it advises against all travel to several provinces, including North Kivu and South Kivu.

payments.text: The UK says credit cards are accepted only in a limited number of places in Kinshasa and other cities, that US dollars are widely used alongside the local currency, and that cash is needed for transactions elsewhere. Canada says the DRC is a cash-based economy and that shopkeepers and foreign exchange dealers require US dollar notes in good condition, printed after 2009.

safety.text: Canada says to avoid all travel to the DRC due to the fragile security situation and the outbreak of Ebola disease. The UK advises against all travel to the provinces of Haut-Uélé, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Maniema, Tanganyika and Haut-Lomami, the Kwamouth territory of Mai-Ndombe and within 50km of the Central African Republic border. It says the armed group M23 and Rwanda Defence Forces have captured Goma and Bukavu, and that foreign nationals are at particular risk of street robbery in Kinshasa, Lubumbashi and other urban centres.

tips.text: The UK advises against all travel to several provinces, including North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri, and says the armed group M23 and Rwanda Defence Forces have captured Goma and Bukavu. Canada, which advises against all travel to the DRC, says armed groups control the towns of Goma and Bukavu.

The UK government says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter the DRC, and that you may need one for onward travel to some other countries because of the risk of yellow fever in the DRC.

Canada's travel advice says shopkeepers and foreign exchange dealers require US dollar notes in good condition, printed after 2009, and the UK says cash is needed for transactions outside Kinshasa and other cities.
Canada's travel advice says it is forbidden, under penalty of arrest or detention, to take photographs of government buildings, airports and military installations.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Democratic Republic of the Congo?
faq.answer: The UK, Canadian, Australian and Italian governments say their citizens need a visa, obtained before travel. The immigration service's eVisa portal (evisa.gouv.cd) is open to any foreigner wishing to come for a visit and tourism, and DRC embassies also issue visas. No official source we could read states which other nationalities need a visa or lists visa-exempt nationalities.

faq.question: How does the DRC eVisa work?
faq.answer: Apply on the official portal, evisa.gouv.cd. The immigration service (DGM) says the eVisa lets you present yourself at any DRC entry point, must be used within three months of issue, and entitles you to a single-entry, 7-day extendable airport visa (VAP), which costs USD 90 payable at the entry point.

faq.question: What is the "visa volant"?
faq.answer: It is the DRC eVisa: the immigration service's eVisa FAQ lists the eVisa's types as the specific visa volant, the ordinary visa volant and the visa volant for family visits. The eVisa costs USD 300 and entitles you to a 7-day extendable airport visa (VAP), which costs USD 90 at the entry point.

faq.question: Is the yellow fever vaccine mandatory for the DRC?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government says that to enter the DRC you must have a certificate proving you've had a yellow fever vaccination.

faq.question: Is the DRC safe to visit?
faq.answer: Canada says to avoid all travel to the DRC, and the UK advises against all travel to several provinces, including North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri. Canada says armed groups control the towns of Goma and Bukavu, and that violent demonstrations, sometimes targeting foreign nationals, previously took place in Kinshasa.

faq.question: Do East African Community citizens need a visa for the DRC?
faq.answer: No official source we could read states a visa exemption for EAC citizens: the immigration service's eVisa FAQ names none.
